text: The Marisol Trench probe reached 6,100 metres on Tuesday morning before operators cut power and began recovery, the mission team told the Gazette at the Port Lume dock. I watched the black instrument pod come up beaded with salt and mud, while engineer Leona Vesk pointed to the depth log on a tablet and said the reading held steady at 6,100 metres for nearly nine minutes. The descent started just after 4:20 a.m. and passed the trench’s sheer southern wall before telemetry wavered. Project lead Tomas Arel said the crew received a clean acoustic ping at maximum depth, then brought the probe back “without a scratch.” The team expects to inspect samples by Friday.
